sources.limitation: Defines the user-approved ILIKE search boundary but does not prove the Flutter implementation.
Defines intended behavior, not a running application.
Static documents cannot prove target size, reflow, or semantics.
Browser runner proves contract reachability, not device/runtime behavior.

validationRuns.command: validate_prototype.py prototype.json; validate_ui_prototype_alignment.py --ui-design ui-design.json --prototype prototype.json; validate_prototype_runner.py --html prototype-runner/index.html --prototype prototype.json --design-system design-system.json
validationRuns.evidence: 11 nodes and 16 transitions validated; runner structurally exercised search states.

conditions: Implement and test three Supabase/Postgres ILIKE '%query%' searches over figure names, article titles, and topic names; merge results with their object types.
Implement semantic 44 pt iOS and 48 dp Android hit targets around smaller locked visual controls.
Implement and device-verify saved People-page context across search dismissal and detail Back.
decision.rationale: The package is internally traceable, the main flows have recovery paths, and the user resolved the first-release search scope. Runtime Flutter and device platform behavior remain untested.

findings.title: Search scope is explicitly bounded
findings.evidence: User confirmed that the first release uses Supabase/Postgres ILIKE '%query%' against figure names, article titles, and topic names only; typo tolerance, pinyin, aliases, simplified/traditional conversion, and complex ordering are excluded.
findings.affectedUsers: Users searching figures, article titles, or topic names.
findings.impact: The core discovery task now has a bounded, implementable search promise.
findings.fix: Implement three ILIKE '%query%' queries, merge typed results, and do not add unsupported fuzzy-search behavior.
findings.verification: Focused tests cover the three field queries, substring matches, zero results, failure, retry, and typed-result merge.

findings.title: Locked visual dimensions need explicit semantic hit-area wrappers
findings.evidence: Visible search, filter, and row measurements are below the stated 44 pt iOS and 48 dp Android target guidance unless the implementation adds larger semantic bounds.
findings.affectedUsers: Users with motor impairments and users operating filters/search one-handed.
findings.impact: Directly using visible dimensions as hit areas would make frequent actions error-prone and violate the intended accessibility contract.
findings.fix: Preserve visual dimensions but wrap every interactive component in a non-overlapping 44 pt/48 dp minimum semantic hit area.
findings.verification: Widget tests inspect hit bounds; iOS/Android manual tests confirm adjacent actions remain independently operable at large text.

findings.title: Detail defaults and restoration storage boundary need implementation definition
findings.evidence: Article body is deferred to the existing route, figure detail structure is deferred, and cold-start persistence fields are not decided.
findings.affectedUsers: Readers returning from detail after backgrounding, recreation, or an unavailable target.
findings.impact: Navigation can restore partially or show ambiguous detail states.
findings.fix: Identify existing article/figure routes, define their loading/error ownership, and decide which People-page fields are in-memory versus restoration-persisted.
findings.verification: Widget/integration tests cover existing routes, search close, detail return, resume, and Android recreation against the chosen boundary.

findings.title: Platform and notification policy need device evidence
findings.evidence: All listed platform checks are not-tested and the supported OS/API range plus notification authorization timing are unresolved.
findings.affectedUsers: iOS/Android users using system Back, assistive technology, large text, keyboard, or notification deep links.
findings.impact: Static visual agreement cannot prevent platform behavior regressions.
findings.fix: Record supported OS/API ranges, keep notification permission optional, and run the device matrix after implementation.
findings.verification: Attach iOS/Android evidence for Back, insets, text scaling, assistive tech, reduced motion, recreation, and invalid deep-link recovery.

strengths.evidence: ui-design.json and design-system.json preserve user-selected VD2 as a locked semantic system.
strengths.statement: The visual direction is traceable and does not depend on an unstructured screenshot.

strengths.evidence: ux-architecture.json, prototype.json, and UI/prototype alignment validation cover all four screens and eleven required states.
strengths.statement: Independent filtering, recovery, search close, and detail return have explicit contracts.

strengths.evidence: platform-guidelines.json FB1-FB3 and prototype FH7 define optional notification behavior and People-page fallback.
strengths.statement: Secondary system entry cannot block the core discovery task.

notTested.reason: The user-approved ILIKE scope is documented, but no Flutter/Supabase query or test has yet been implemented.
No Flutter code or widget/integration tests have been created for this package.
No iPhone evidence exists for edge Back, Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, keyboard, safe areas, or Reduce Motion.
No Android evidence exists for predictive Back, insets, font scale, TalkBack, process recreation, or adaptive windows.
